name: Burson-Marsteller

summary.text: Burson-Marsteller was a public relations and public affairs firm co-founded in 1953 by Harold Burson and advertising executive Bill Marsteller. It was sold to Young & Rubicam in 1979, which WPP acquired in 2000. In 2018 WPP merged Burson-Marsteller with Cohn & Wolfe to form Burson Cohn & Wolfe (BCW), and in 2024 merged BCW with Hill & Knowlton to form Burson. In 1993 the firm's grassroots-lobbying unit created the National Smokers Alliance on behalf of Philip Morris; the Alliance's president was a Burson-Marsteller vice president.

sources.title: WPP merges BCW and Hill & Knowlton to create Burson

facts.claim: Burson-Marsteller was co-founded in 1953 by Harold Burson and advertising executive Bill Marsteller. Burson sold the firm to Young & Rubicam in 1979; Young & Rubicam was bought by WPP in 2000.
facts.quote: Harold Burson co-founded Burson-Marsteller in 1953 with ad executive Bill Marsteller. In 1979, Burson sold the firm to ad agency Young & Rubicam, which was in turn bought by WPP in 2000.

sources.title: WPP merges BCW and Hill & Knowlton to create Burson

facts.claim: In 2018 WPP merged Burson-Marsteller, then the sixth-largest PR firm worldwide, with Cohn & Wolfe, ranked twelfth, to form Burson Cohn & Wolfe (BCW), the third-largest PR firm.
facts.quote: in 2018 parent company WPP merged Burson-Marsteller, the sixth-largest PR firm worldwide, and Cohn & Wolfe, which ranked 12th. The result was the third-largest PR firm, which was named Burson Cohn & Wolfe (BCW).

facts.claim: In January 2024 WPP announced the merger of BCW with Hill & Knowlton to form a new agency named Burson; the merger was finalized in July 2024. Harold Burson died in 2020 at 98.
facts.quote: In January 2024, WPP announced plans to merge BCW with Hill & Knowlton, forming the new agency, Burson. The merger was finalized in July 2024.

sources.title: WPP merges BCW and Hill & Knowlton to create Burson

facts.claim: In 1992 Burson-Marsteller set up a grassroots-lobbying unit called the Advocacy Communications Team; in 1993 that team created the National Smokers Alliance on behalf of Philip Morris.
facts.quote: In 1992, the PR company set up a unit specialised in grassroots lobbying called the Advocacy Communications Team. The following year, in 1993, this team created the National Smokers Alliance on behalf of Philip Morris.

facts.claim: The National Smokers Alliance's president was a vice president of Burson-Marsteller, and other Burson-Marsteller executives were involved in the organisation; the names of the group's corporate funders and organisers were kept off its materials.
facts.quote: The Alliance's president was the vice president of Burson-Marsteller, and other Burson-Marsteller executives were actively involved in the organisation.

facts.claim: A 2017 law-firm article, citing a SAC report, identified Thomas Humber, a Burson-Marsteller executive, as nominal head of the National Smokers Alliance and said Philip Morris founded it with an initial contribution of $7 million to Burson-Marsteller.
facts.quote: Philip Morris founded it with an initial contribution of $7 million dollars to Burson-Marsteller.

sources.title: Why Philip Morris Hates Trial Lawyers

facts.claim: A Philip Morris record dated October 7, 1993 in the UCSF Truth Tobacco Industry Documents archive, filed under the label "TOBACCO - NAT'L. SMOKER'S ALLIANCE," is catalogued as an outline, presentation, report and speech on the National Smokers Alliance.

sources.title: National Smokers Alliance Overview (Philip Morris Records)

facts.claim: The first issue of the National Smokers Alliance's monthly bulletin (November 1993) includes a founder's account stating that in August he sent letters to every major cigarette manufacturer requesting start-up funding and support.
facts.quote: in August, I sent letters to every major cigarette manufacturer requesting start-up funding and support.

sources.title: Monthly Bulletin of the National Smokers Alliance, November 1993, Vol. 1 Issue 1

openQuestions: Funding figures for the National Smokers Alliance differ by source ($4 million seed money per Americans for Nonsmokers' Rights; $7 million initial contribution per a SAC report cited by Howarth & Smith; the site's '$42 million in first four years'); none was confirmed from a Philip Morris document.
The 1953 founding and 1979 Young & Rubicam sale should be confirmed against a primary biography or WPP filing.
The full text of UCSF document lkdm0127 was not read; only its catalogue metadata was available.
